items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to ensuring insurance coverage for children in need of early intervention services
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5175

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the insurance law, in relation
to ensuring insurance coverage for children in
need of early intervention services

PURPOSE:
To ensure insurance coverage for children ages 0-3 in need of early
intervention services.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
Section 1 amends section 3235-a to delineate conditions for
preapproval of early intervention

Section 2 designates the effective date for the bill after it shall
have become a law.

EXISTING LAW: None.

JUSTIFICATION:
The Early Intervention Program offers a variety of therapeutic and
support services to eligible infants and toddlers with disabilities
aged 0 - 3.

Last year, of the participating families in children in EIP, about 48%
of recipients had private insurance. Counties then billed third party
providers $100 million for school-district mandated services. Of the
$100 million billed, only $10 million was received. 10% paid on what
is 100% justifiably owed. The justification for such disparity
between monies owed and monies received includes nothing to help
these children with the most difficult of obstacles. In fact, it does
the very opposite.

The only thing accomplished when reimbursement is denied is a heavier
cost burden on the shoulders of counties. From top to bottom, the
Early Intervention Program is undermined, if not altogether dropped
because the necessary funds cannot be allocated. This legislation bans
insurance companies from denying Early Intervention claims based on
most of the common reasons.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New Bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None to the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply to any
contracts entered into, altered, modified, extended or removed on or
after such effective date.
